title: Wimbledon Boss Jokes Security Would Stop Disruptive Influencers
summary:
Wimbledon's boss joked that military guards at the tennis club would love to "sort out" social media influencers who interrupt matches. He also said influencers still matter for marketing today.

The talk follows a problem at the U.S. Open, where about 100 influencers got special passes. A photo shoot during a Naomi Osaka match stopped play and started a debate about manners at tennis. Star Coco Gauff said new fans are welcome but should follow the sport's etiquette.

Wimbledon's Atkinson said the club has no official "influencer" pass group. Brand partners may bring creators, but they would be closely watched. He likes Wimbledon's quiet tradition of fans respecting the game.

Fans may not bring portable ring lights. Atkinson said a total ban on influencers would be silly, but Wimbledon will handle them "in a Wimbledon way" to keep the tournament's special feel.
why_it_matters: Kids can talk about how online fame and real-world manners should share sports spaces.
